extracted.intended_audience: TikTok creators, social media managers, and marketers trying to maximize distribution on the For You Page
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and metrics for creating, formatting, and publishing TikTok videos to maximize recommendation-driven reach (For You Page) in 2026, including ranking signals, distribution phases, content formats, and posting tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest graph (content-first recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok uses an interest graph, not a social graph — it recommends content based on what you'll enjoy, not who you follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains why creators with zero followers can get huge reach; platform prioritizes predicted enjoyment over follower relationships. Use content that matches viewer interests rather than relying on network ties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation system goal & five-step pipeline
rubrics_metrics.description: The system's stated goal is to maximize watch time and engagement by showing the right content to the right person at the right time. Creator Academy describes a five-step process: Selecting videos, Prediction, Ranking, Similarity check, Recommendation rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that videos are filtered by interest and context, predicted for engagement, ranked by score, de-duplicated for variety, and finally subject to regional/diversity rules — optimize content and metadata for each stage (e.g., clear topic, strong early engagement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking signal categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Three categories of signals determine FYP ranking: User Interactions (Strongest), Video Information (Medium), Device & Account Settings (Weakest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize signals in that order when optimizing: engagement behaviors first, then content metadata (captions/hashtags/audio), and lastly device/locale factors which have minimal weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: User Interactions (Strongest Signal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tracks videos you've watched/finished/liked/shared/skipped, follows, comments, content created, and likelihood to engage with specific types of content. TikTok: 'A strong indicator of interest, such as whether a user finishes watching a longer video from beginning to end, would receive greater weight than a weak indicator.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design for engagement behaviors (completion, rewatch, shares, saves, meaningful comments). Early follower engagement is now used as a testbed (see phased distribution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Video Information (Medium Signal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithm analyzes captions/on-screen text, hashtags/keywords, sounds/music, effects/filters, and content topic/category via AI vision and NLP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimize captions, on-screen text, and audio to be keyword-relevant; use meaningful hashtags and original audio where possible to improve discovery and search relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Device & Account Settings (Weakest Signal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Baseline context like region/country, language preference, device type and OS are considered but carry minimal weight because 'users don't actively express them as preferences.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are not primary levers; only ensure metadata aligns with target audience locale and language for baseline relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watch time & completion rate weight (~40-50%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch time and completion rate are the #1 ranking factor, estimated to account for ~40-50% of algorithmic weight. The completion rate bar for virality is ~70% in 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design videos to maximize retention — strong hooks, tight edits, and clear payoffs so you exceed the ~70% completion threshold for viral distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-watch rate importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-watch rate is rated 'Very high' — immediate replays signal exceptional quality and provide a massive visibility boost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create content with looping appeal or surprise/complexity that encourages replays (ambiguous endings, reveal moments, or dense info that viewers rewatch).

rubrics_metrics.name: Shares (Very high)
rubrics_metrics.description: Shares are 'Very high' importance and now outweigh likes; shares per post increased year-over-year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize creating content people want to send to friends — emotional hooks, clear value, or social currency prompts help increase share rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saves (Very high)
rubrics_metrics.description: Saves are treated as a stronger relevance indicator than likes and are classified as 'Very high'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce evergreen, referenceable, or tutorial-style content that viewers will save for later; explicitly prompt saves when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments (High; quality-weighted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments are high-value but quality-weighted — one thoughtful ~50-word comment outweighs multiple emoji responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage substantive discussion with prompts or questions; avoid strategies that solicit low-value reactions only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Likes (Moderate; declining)
rubrics_metrics.description: Likes remain a signal but their importance is moderate and declining after recent updates that deprioritize 'shallow interactions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not focus on likes as the primary metric; optimize for deeper engagement signals instead (completion, shares, saves, comments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Original audio priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Original audio is a growing signal — TikTok rewards original sounds over borrowed/trending sounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, create original audio or voiceover content to get a ranking boost. Use trending audio strategically but favor originality for long-term visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original content policy (watermarked repost suppression)
rubrics_metrics.description: Original content is valued highly. Watermarked reposts from other platforms get suppressed in distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid posting watermarked cross-platform content; create native videos or remove watermarks before posting to prevent suppression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production quality (Moderate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Production quality (lighting, sound, editing) is a newly considered signal with moderate importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improve basic production elements to avoid penalties to watch time and engagement; you don't need cinematic quality but ensure clear audio and good lighting/edit pacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phased distribution system (4 phases) / Phase 1: Follower-first testing
rubrics_metrics.description: New videos are distributed in phases. Phase 1 (2026 change) shows new videos primarily to your existing followers to evaluate completion, shares, and saves before broader distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because follower engagement now gates broader reach, post when your followers are active and can provide early completion/share/save signals; encourage rapid follower interaction in the first hours/days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phased distribution: Audience Expansion, Virality, Plateau
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase 2 expands to larger non-follower waves if initial metrics are strong; Phase 3 is virality when engagement snowballs; Phase 4 is plateau/decline as audience segments are exhausted or engagement drops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design content to perform consistently across waves (not just an initial spike). Series content and strong middle-to-end retention help sustain expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithm does NOT consider follower count as a direct factor
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok has officially stated follower count is not a direct ranking factor; previous high-performing videos do not directly boost future content; new accounts can go viral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't rely on follower count to seed reach; focus on making each video earn engagement signals independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimal video length by goal
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended lengths: Maximum virality 11-18s; Maximum engagement 15-30s; Storytelling 21-34s; Educational/tutorial up to 60s; Monetization 60+ seconds; Longer-form 60-180s is growing. Key insight: length matters less than retention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose length based on goal but prioritize completion rate — a 3-minute video with 80% completion can outperform a 15s video with 40% completion. Export at proper resolution to avoid compression issues that harm watch time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content types that perform best
rubrics_metrics.description: High-performing formats: educational/informational with a strong hook, behind-the-scenes/authentic content, storytelling with narrative arc, interactive content (questions/polls/challenges), duets & stitches, original audio/voiceover, and series content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt content mix recommendation: 70% value/entertainment, 20% interactive/community-building, 10% direct promotional. Focus on strong hooks and formats that drive rewatch/shares/saves.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3-second rule (hook quickly)
rubrics_metrics.description: You have three seconds to hook viewers. Keeping them past three seconds substantially increases FYP ranking chances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with a question, preview of payoff, or striking visuals; never a slow intro. Use captions/on-screen text in the first 2-3 seconds to capture attention and help TikTok OCR.

rubrics_metrics.name: TikTok features that affect ranking: Duets
rubrics_metrics.description: Duets pair your content with a trending/high-visibility original, piggybacking on existing momentum and exposing you to audiences who found the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use duets to reach audiences of popular creators; ensure your take adds value and retains viewers to maximize completion and shares.

rubrics_metrics.name: TikTok features that affect ranking: Stitches
rubrics_metrics.description: Stitches embed your voice into existing conversations; perceived as an extension of dialogue and tends to retain viewership longer, boosting average watch time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stitch contextually relevant clips and add succinct, value-adding commentary that encourages completion and rewatch.

rubrics_metrics.name: TikTok LIVE ranking signals
rubrics_metrics.description: LIVE content promotion is based on real-time engagement. Post-2025 updates emphasize completion rate (percentage watching most of the LIVE), product interaction diversity, and comment quality (substantive questions > simple reactions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During LIVE, drive sustained viewership, encourage diverse interactions (gifts, purchases, chat), and solicit substantive comments to improve distribution and monetization access.

rubrics_metrics.name: TikTok Shop & live shopping
rubrics_metrics.description: In-app purchasing integration; live shopping events generate ~22% higher conversion rates than standard product videos and e-commerce is core to TikTok in 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If selling, use live shopping events and native TikTok Shop features to boost conversion and algorithmic visibility for commerce content.

rubrics_metrics.name: TikTok SEO (captions, on-screen text, voiceover, profile)
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok operates as a search engine; captions, on-screen text (OCR), and spoken words are scanned for keywords. Key placement: captions (first 150 characters), on-screen text within the first 2-3 seconds, voiceover mentioning keywords early, and profile name/bio optimized for niche terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write captions as search queries (natural language). Place keywords early in visuals and audio to improve discoverability; use profile/bio for niche keyword matches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting frequency & timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended frequency 3-5 posts per week (Buffer data: biggest lift from 1 to 2-5/week). Best times: 7-9 AM, 12-1 PM, 6-9 PM local time; peak windows vary by content type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistency matters more than volume. Post when followers are most active because follower-first testing now gates broader distribution. Use scheduling tools to hit these windows and be present to engage within the first hour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hashtag strategy (3-5 relevant tags)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 3-5 highly relevant hashtags per post (1-2 broad tags, 2-3 niche tags, 1-2 content-specific tags). Avoid hashtag stuffing and generic tags like #fyp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine hashtags with caption keywords. Avoid irrelevant tags that confuse the algorithm; use generators or research to find niche tags with engaged audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caption and keyword optimization
rubrics_metrics.description: Captions now matter more than hashtags for discovery. Keywords in captions can boost visibility by 20-40%. Write captions the way users search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put primary keywords in the first 150 characters and write natural, searchable phrases (e.g., 'morning skincare routine for sensitive skin'). Consider AI caption tools but review for search intent accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content tactics & engagement behaviors
rubrics_metrics.description: Tactical checklist: Hook within 3s; optimize for completion rate (aim ~70%); prioritize shares and saves over likes; use original audio; reply to comments with video; post Duets/Stitches; build series content; optimize for search. 'Watch time and completion rate account for 40-50% of the algorithm.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement these tactics together — e.g., start with a 3s hook, include on-screen keywords, encourage saves/shares, and follow-up by replying with video to extend content lifecycle and generate more watch-time signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Myths debunked guiding principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifications that inform strategy: deleting underperforming videos won't improve future reach; watching your own video doesn't boost it; shadowbanning isn't an acknowledged mechanism; there's no secret 'hack' — focus on measured signals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid reactive behaviors based on myths (mass-deleting content, obsessing over timing hacks). Concentrate on signals the algorithm actually measures and long-term content quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform transition guidance (Oracle/US retraining)
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithm retraining on US data (Oracle deal) may cause distribution fluctuations through mid-2026, but fundamentals (watch time, completion, shares) remain core signals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During algorithm retraining periods, focus on fundamentals and expect short-term visibility shifts; do not overhaul strategy based solely on transitional noise.
